author: OSaMaBiNLoGiN
headline: AI-idle developer expects layoff, plans OnlyFans or a cool drug habit
summary: The developer who lets AI do his job says the dev team is pointless and jokes he will start an OnlyFans or get addicted to drugs.
evidence: Not hiring. I'm pretty sure I only have a job for a couple more months. I don't see the point of having a dev team, and I'm on the dev team. Then I'll start an onlyfans or get addicted to some cool drug. Not sure.

author: OSaMaBiNLoGiN
headline: Employer knows he lets AI work while he games, keeps him anyway
summary: The video-gaming developer says his employer is fully aware and keeps him for 'product-shaping ideas' he himself can't define.
evidence:
Employer is fully aware. I'm kept around because I provide a "valuable perspective" and regularly have "product-shaping ideas".

I don't know what either of those two things actually mean.

author: drgoodvibe
headline: Solo builder averages about 40 billion tokens per month
summary: Running three Claude Ultra accounts, Codex Pro and local GPU rigs, one person reports averaging around 40 billion tokens a month.
evidence: 3x Claude ultra, codex pro, + local Qwen 27b fp8 on Radiance engine on 2xRS700 and ComfyUi on a separate machine with a rtx 4090. It’s been super fun building everything. I’ve averaged around ~40B tokens per month..

author: Rilup
headline: Approved key-lookup bug silently published captures without proof for a day
summary: A non-programmer founder approved agent code he didn't understand, and a bug published user captures without their proof for a full day.
evidence: The two incidents that hurt most were the times I skipped that step and approved something without understanding it: a `git add -A` that deleted half the website, and a key-lookup bug that silently published captures without their proof for a day.

author: bsenftner
headline: Runs 318 local generative models alongside an OpenAI subscription
summary: One developer hosts 318 local generative models for text, image, voice, music and video, managed through WanGP and two self-written apps.
evidence: 2) Current count, 318 additional generative models across LLMs and then media generation of image, voice, music and video. The LLMs are mostly Qwen variants, and the media models are pretty much all the popular media models.

author: OSaMaBiNLoGiN
headline: Doubted AI-slacker replies with his 62% Xerath winrate
summary: Told his story of letting AI do his job while gaming was made up, he cites his League of Legends win rate as proof.
evidence: Tell that to my 62% Xerath winrate. I'm fucking owning.

author: la_balce
headline: Solo CTO's agents ship to prod with no human code review
summary: A startup CTO's agent pipeline plans, tests, audits, merges and watches production on its own, with hooks blocking prod writes, Stripe and emails.
evidence:
A shipper merges and watches prod for 15 min. - Opus judges, Sonnet implements, escalate to Opus on the 3rd failure. A judge is never weaker than what it judges. - I make 2 decisions per mission, as multiple-choice questions. Most missions ship the same day; every friction becomes a rule or a test.

The trade-off: no human code review, compensated by automated checks.

author: spilist
headline: 'Team Leader' agent orchestrates six machines across three operating systems
summary: With five coding subscriptions, one orchestrator agent called 'Team Leader' drives agents on six Linux, macOS and Windows machines over Tailscale.
evidence: 1) Codex $200 * 2, Claude Code $200, Muse Code $50, OpenCode $40. I run them in 6 machines (2 Linux, 2 MacOS, 2 Windows)

author: shepherdjerred
headline: Seven AI subscriptions at once, about $500 a month
summary: One person pays for Claude, ChatGPT, SuperGrok, Kimi, Cursor, Google AI and Muse Code at once, about $500 monthly, and still hits limits.
evidence: 1. Claude Ultra, ChatGPT Pro 200, SuperGrok, Kimi Pro, Cursor Pro, Google AI Pro, Muse Code High Usage. It comes out to ~$500/mo, mostly from Claude+ChatGPT

author: Wolfbeta
headline: ChatGPT shell commands copied to clipboard, intercepted by Hammerspoon and executed
summary: To dodge rate limits, ChatGPT writes shell payloads that Hammerspoon grabs from the clipboard, validates and runs on local or remote machines.
evidence: ChatGPT generates shell payloads that I copy into the clipboard. Hammerspoon intercepts them, validates them against an explicit contract, and dispatches them to local or remote execution environments. Interactive workloads run in tmux, and the resulting transcripts are delivered back into ChatGPT.
